 General Election Results to be Audited at 49 Selected Voting Precincts
 Routine post-election audits are one of many safeguards protecting Connecticut voters 
 (Hartford, Connecticut) — The Office of the Secretary of the State today randomly selected 49 precincts from the November 3, 2026, General Election to have their machine totals audited. Seventeen alternates were also chosen. These routine post-election audits are one of many safeguards designed to ensure votes are counted accurately.
 Connecticut General Statutes § 9‑320f requires that five percent of all voting precincts have their machine totals audited. There were 973 precincts used during the General Election.
 Bipartisan local election officials in the 49 selected precincts will now re-tabulate the voter-marked paper ballots and compare those results with what the tabulators reported on Election Day.
 “We don't wait to hear about something going wrong before we go back and check our results,” said Secretary of the State Stephanie Thomas . “I've talked all election season about people, paper, and proof. Now we're at the paper and proof stage: going back to our paper ballots and checking whether the machines counted them accurately.”
 Officials in the selected precincts must complete their audits by November 23 and submit their reports to the Office of the Secretary of the State. The reports will then be forwarded to the University of Connecticut for independent analysis.
 UConn's findings will be returned to the Secretary's Office and filed with the State Elections Enforcement Commission (SEEC). The findings will also be made available to the public.
